task.name: A role whose output is only usable when structured is assigned to a model that cannot produce it, so the gate depending on that output presents no recommendation and cannot say why
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2466
---

**Depends on #2466.** This issue's assignment guard has to consult whether a model has demonstrated it can return a structured result. #2466 is what makes that fact durable and readable at dispatch.

Corrected 2026-08-15: this previously pointed at #2378, on the reading that a readiness check reporting per-capability outcomes would also record them. #2378 has since landed and does not — it exercises the capability correctly and reports to whoever invoked it, persisting nothing that any runtime path reads. Preflight refused this story on exactly that basis, correctly, before any development began. Reporting to an operator and recording for a router are different things, and the original edge conflated them.

## Observed

A story reached the escalate gate. The gate ran its advisor, the advisor produced output, and the
gate then presented its full set of operator actions with no recommendation attached and no
indication that the advisory step had failed rather than declined.

The advisor had been assigned to a model whose transport rejected the structured tool-call request.
The run fell back to plain text, which cannot carry the structured report the gate requires, so
report validation failed and the gate recorded the advisory as unavailable. The advisory step
consumed wall clock and spend and returned nothing usable.

Because there was no recommendation, the expiry path had nothing to apply and preserved the
checkpoint for an operator instead. The story had already been marked failed by then, so the
preserved decision was for work no longer running.

The model carried an explicit eligibility restriction in project configuration naming the phases it
was allowed to serve. That restriction did not prevent this assignment, because the advisor role is
not one of the phases the restriction vocabulary can express.

## Expected

A role whose result is only usable as a structured artifact is assigned only to a model able to
produce that artifact. Where no eligible model can, the role reports that it could not run, and the
step that depends on it states that its input is missing rather than presenting a degraded result as
a complete one. A step that produces nothing usable is not silently indistinguishable from a step
that ran and had nothing to say.

Eligibility declared for a model governs every role that model can be assigned. Where a role sits
outside the vocabulary those declarations use, it is nameable in that vocabulary, so a restriction an
operator writes cannot be silently narrower than the set of jobs the model will actually be given.

## Diagnosis

**Observed symptom.** The escalate gate offered its operator actions with no advisory recommendation, and the
advisory-unavailable state was reached through a failure rather than an absence of opinion.

**Evidence.**

- `src/theforge/config/model_identity.py:79` — `KNOWN_PHASES` is `frozenset({"preflight", "dev",
  "plan", "review"})`. The advisor role is not a member, so it cannot appear in a
  `routing.phase_eligibility` list.
- `src/theforge/config/model_catalog.py:303` — parsed phases are rejected when outside
  `KNOWN_PHASES`, so an operator cannot name the advisor role even deliberately.
- Run log, escalate gate on one story: the advisor start line, then a transport error on the
  tool-call request and a fallback to single-shot text mode, then
  `advisory report failed validation: ['no <advisory_report> block found in advisor output']`.
- The resulting pending record carries `advisory_unavailable: true` alongside the full options list.

**Ruled out.** Not the advisor prompt: the advisor was reached and produced output. Not the report
validator: it correctly rejected text with no report block. Not the expiry path, which behaved as
specified — it had no recommendation to apply. Not operator configuration error: the restriction the
operator wrote was accepted by config validation and simply does not reach this role.

**Confirmed cause.** Advisor assignment draws from the eligible model set without requiring the
capability its output format depends on, and the eligibility vocabulary cannot express the advisor
role, so neither the automatic path nor an operator override can keep an unsuitable model out of it.

**Affected code path.** Advisor model selection, the tool-call-to-text fallback in the transport
layer, and advisory report validation at the escalate gate.

**Fix-success criterion.** A model that cannot produce the advisor's structured output is not given
the advisor role; when the role cannot be filled, the gate states that the advisory is missing and
why, and that state is distinguishable from an advisor that ran and returned no recommendation.

handoff.summary: Implemented advisor-aware assignment gating and gate-state reporting for escalation advice. The advisor role is now nameable in phase eligibility, defaults and shipped explicit model lists include it where appropriate, and advisor dispatch consults the durable structured-output capability record before contacting a model. When no eligible structured-capable advisor exists, the coordinator records and persists a distinct unavailable reason, the pending escalate gate renders that as missing advisory input, and audit/resume preserve it. I also extended advisory parsing so a valid 'no recommendation' result is distinct from unavailable advice, and added seam-level regression coverage across config parsing, advisor dispatch, pending gate rendering, and resume/audit persistence.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 says to add advisor only to KNOWN_PHASES, but src/theforge/config/model_identity.py separately defines _DEFAULT_PHASE_ELIGIBILITY as {preflight, dev, plan, review}. Step 3 then requires the reused preflight default to pass advisor eligibility, so every model relying on default eligibility would be rejected. This carries the plan's stated preflight-default compatibility risk and would make advisor assignment unavailable for ordinary existing configurations.
  Suggestion: Add advisor to _DEFAULT_PHASE_ELIGIBILITY as well as KNOWN_PHASES, and test both an unrestricted/default model remaining advisor-eligible and an explicitly restricted model being excluded.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Steps 3–4 do not identify a viable phase-eligibility data path. config.agents contains AgentDef objects, but AgentDef in src/theforge/config/models.py does not carry phase_eligibility; that field exists on AgentSpec/ModelInfo and is consumed by config/role_derivation.py. assign_models() also has no advisor role or advisor field in AssignmentDecision. Merely adding advisor to ROLE_REQUIRED_CAPABILITY cannot make the shared assignment guard apply advisor eligibility.
  Suggestion: Specify the single-role advisor selector explicitly: either extend the registry-backed helpers in config/role_derivation.py with fail-closed advisor filtering and then apply the #2466 capability lookup, or propagate eligibility into the assignment candidate type and add a dedicated shared role-selection API. Include the additional affected files and a test proving an explicit eligibility restriction reaches runtime selection.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Steps 4–5 require a 'successfully parsed' or 'valid' advisory report with no recommendation, but parse_advisory_report() in src/theforge/escalation_advisor.py requires recommendation to be in ACTION_TAXONOMY; an empty recommendation necessarily sets parse_errors, making AdvisoryReport.ok false. The planned regression can therefore only construct an impossible object directly and would not cover the runtime parser path.
  Suggestion: Either include escalation_advisor.py and deliberately extend its schema to represent a valid declined/no-recommendation result, or restate the distinction using realizable states such as no_eligible_model, invocation_failed, and report_validation_failed, with tests passing actual text through parse_advisory_report().
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 4 introduces an explicit advisor-unavailable reason but lists neither coordinator/state.py nor its durable consumers in coordinator/resume_persistence.py and coordinator/audit.py. The existing advisory_launch_* fields specifically mean the process failed before contacting a model and should not be overloaded for capability or eligibility refusal.
  Suggestion: Add a dedicated unavailable-reason field to CoordinatorState, persist and restore it in the escalation resume block, include it in audit output, and test the live and resumed pending-gate rendering.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 adds advisor to KNOWN_PHASES but leaves _DEFAULT_PHASE_ELIGIBILITY (model_identity.py:181, frozenset{preflight,dev,plan,review}) and the shipped catalog untouched, while Step 3 makes advisor selection fail closed. Every builtin entry in src/theforge/config/data/models.yaml that declares an explicit list — [preflight, review] (lines 121, 220), [dev, plan, review] (line 361) — and every model taking the default would then be advisor-ineligible, so the pool empties and the gate reports 'no structured-capable advisor model available' on every escalation. This is the plan's own stated risk 3 ('may affect existing operator assumptions'), and its mitigation ('only reuse preflight defaults after they pass advisor eligibility') is what causes the failure rather than retiring it. It is also unlike role_derivation._phase_candidates (role_derivation.py:117), which falls back to the full list when filtering empties it — so no existing behaviour rescues this.
  Suggestion: Decide the semantics in the plan and test it: either (a) add advisor to _DEFAULT_PHASE_ELIGIBILITY and to every builtin models.yaml entry intended to serve it, or (b) treat a declaration that does not mention advisor as unrestricted for advisor (only an explicit exclusion removes a model), with capability, not phase, as the binding filter. State which, and add a test asserting that a default forge.yaml with the shipped catalog still produces an eligible advisor.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Adding advisor to ROLE_REQUIRED_CAPABILITY changes data existing tests iterate: tests/test_capability_routing_seam.py:538 and :583 build explicit_profiles from dict.fromkeys(ROLE_REQUIRED_CAPABILITY, ...) and pass it into assign_models, which knows only the roles hard-coded at assignment.py:3672 (preflight, planner, dev, plan_review, code_review). An advisor key would flow into locked_roles/explicit_profiles on a path that never routes that role.
  Suggestion: Have Step 2 decide whether advisor participates in assign_models' role loop or is filtered only by the advisor flow, and update the seam test's role enumeration accordingly rather than letting it pick up the new key implicitly.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3 says 'shared assignment logic' without naming an entry point; assignment.py exposes no single-role selector — the reusable pieces are _capability_exclusions / _capability_pool / NoCapableCandidateError (assignment.py:397/472/435), and the advisor flow currently receives only state, config, task, workspace_path, so it must pull config.agents and load capability records itself (the pattern at plan_flow.py:640).
  Suggestion: Name the seam explicitly: load load_capabilities(capabilities_path(config.project_root)) in run_escalation_advisor and reuse the existing exclusion helpers, rather than inventing a parallel selector.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 1 (capability constant naming) is retired — CAPABILITY_TOOL_STRUCTURED exists at model_capabilities.py:57 and is already the value used in ROLE_REQUIRED_CAPABILITY. Risk 2 (advisor vs escalation_advisor) is retired by Step 1's config-parsing tests; note only that KNOWN_PHASES holds phase names (plan, review) while ROLE_REQUIRED_CAPABILITY holds role names (plan_review, code_review), so advisor will be the one token appearing in both vocabularies.
  Suggestion: Add a one-line comment at both definitions noting the deliberate name coincidence so the next reader does not treat it as drift.

findings.description: The Expected section states two distinct requirements: (1) a role whose output must be structured is only assigned to a capable model, with missing advisory distinguishable from a null recommendation, and (2) eligibility declarations a model carries must be expressible for every role including advisor, so operator restrictions cannot be silently narrower than actual assignments. The Fix-success criterion only restates requirement (1) — it does not require extending the eligibility vocabulary to include the advisor role. A fix could satisfy the stated success criterion (block incapable models from the advisor role, report missing advisory clearly) while leaving KNOWN_PHASES unable to name the advisor role, which is the second half of Expected and part of the confirmed cause ('the eligibility vocabulary cannot express the advisor role, so ... an operator override can[not] keep an unsuitable model out of it').

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Treat the escalation advisor as a first-class assignable role: make it nameable in model eligibility, require the durable structured-output capability from #2466 before dispatch, and surface capability-blocked advisory absence distinctly at the gate.

steps.description: Add the advisor role to the model eligibility vocabulary.
steps.details: Add `advisor` to `KNOWN_PHASES` so `routing.phase_eligibility` can explicitly allow or exclude advisor assignments. Preserve existing strict rejection for unknown names, and add or update config parsing tests proving `advisor` is accepted while unrelated unknown phases still fail.

steps.description: Require demonstrated structured-output capability for advisor assignment.
steps.details: Extend the existing role-to-capability gating path so the advisor role requires the structured tool/result capability made durable by #2466. Do not create a separate capability source; use the existing demonstrated-capability lookup from `model_capabilities.py`. Cover rejection of an otherwise eligible model that lacks the structured capability.

steps.description: Route escalation advisor model selection through the shared assignment guard.
steps.details: Replace the direct reuse of `config.preflight_profile` in `run_escalation_advisor()` with shared assignment logic that applies both `phase_eligibility: advisor` and the structured-capability requirement. If no eligible model exists, do not call `run_agent`; return the existing advisory-unavailable path with a specific launch/fill failure reason indicating no structured-capable advisor model was available.

steps.description: Make pending HITL output distinguish missing advisory input from no recommendation.
steps.details: Thread the explicit advisor-unavailable reason into the pending escalate record and rendered operator text. Ensure capability-blocked or assignment-blocked advisor absence is reported as missing input with why, while a successfully parsed advisory report with no recommendation remains a separate no-recommendation outcome.

steps.description: Add seam-level regression coverage for the escalation gate boundary.
steps.details: Add integration-style tests around the escalation advisor/gate boundary showing: an ineligible structured-incapable model is not contacted, pending HITL records the missing advisory reason, and a valid advisor run that returns no recommendation remains distinguishable from advisory-unavailable.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A role whose result is only usable as a structured artifact is assigned only to a model able to produce that artifact.
Where no eligible model can, the role reports that it could not run, and the step that depends on it states that its input is missing rather than presenting a degraded result as a complete one.
A step that produces nothing usable is not silently indistinguishable from a step that ran and had nothing to say.

Eligibility declared for a model governs every role that model can be assigned. Where a role sits outside the vocabulary those declarations use, it is nameable in that vocabulary, so a restriction an operator writes cannot be silently narrower than the set of jobs the model will actually be given.

risks.description: The exact capability constant or lookup introduced by #2466 may differ from the preflight summary naming.
risks.mitigation: Have the dev agent use the existing durable capability API in `model_capabilities.py` as the source of truth rather than adding a parallel flag or transport heuristic.

risks.description: The role name could be ambiguous between `advisor` and a longer name such as `escalation_advisor`.
risks.mitigation: Use `advisor` because the spec names the role that way and it keeps `phase_eligibility` concise; document it in the same validation/tests that define the accepted vocabulary.

risks.description: Changing advisor selection from `preflight_profile` reuse may affect existing operator assumptions.
risks.mitigation: Keep fallback behavior explicit: only reuse preflight defaults after they pass advisor eligibility and capability checks, and fail closed with an auditable reason when they do not.
